newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast spot products continue up with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast spot products continue up with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices edged up Monday with higher energy futures markets, traders said.
September unleaded gasoline on the New York Mercantile Exchanged (NYMEX) jumped 1.67 cents a gallon to 66.74 cents, while crude oil for the same delivery month rose 47 cents a barrel to $20.75.
The rally came on the heels of production shut-downs at Occidental's Cano Limon oil field in Colombia, which forced the West Coast-based oil giant to cancel some deliveries.

The stronger futures market influenced West Coast spot prices, with CARB regular unleaded gasoline rising one cent a gallon to 72/73 cents a gallon, a slowdown after last week's 10 percent climb in spot gasoline. CARB diesel fule traded between 65/66 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, up a half cent.
"A very strong Merc (NYMEX) is pulling everything up," a trader said.
Other products rose between one and two cents.
